title: hitop — R package for HiTOP Society questionnaire instruments
text: Scores, validity-screens, distributes HiTOP Society instruments: PID-5 (FULL 220 / SF 100 / BF 25, one function per task version argument), HiTOP-SR (405), HiTOP-BR (45), HiTOP-HSUM (item data + export ; scoring pending Society feedback). Version 0.2.0, GPL-3. Maintained Jeffrey Girard.

title: hitop — R package for HiTOP Society questionnaire instruments
text: Scoring signature: (data, items, [version,] srange, prefix, missing, calc_se, append = TRUE); always returns tibble. id/scales/tibble arguments; scales computed. Reliability separate returning family reliability_{pid5,hitopsr,hitopbr}(data, items, [version,] srange, alpha, omega) → per-scale tibble. Output columns: prefix + camelCase scale name (pid_anhedonia, hsr_...); validity scales prefix + abbreviation (pid_PNA, pid_INC); standard errors add _se. Scale membership comes *_scales list-column tables (pid_scales[[version]]$itemNumbers, hitopsr_scales, hitopbr_scales); reverse-keying validity-scale membership *_items tables. Never hardcode item numbers. User messaging via cli::cli_alert_warning() + cli::cli_alert_info() actionable {.code dplyr::filter(...)} suggestions — except reports caller meant catch suppress, cli::cli_warn() conditions (D-024/D-025 carve-, see DESIGN “User communication”); validation via validate_*()/cli_assert() R/util.R. Base-R data manipulation internally; {tibble} Import (default output), {lavaan} Suggests (needed calc_omega). Instrument administration text lives R/sysdata.rda (*_instructions); prebuilt DOCX/Qualtrics/REDCap artifacts inst/extdata/.

title: Compute Cronbach's Coefficient Alpha — calc_alpha
text: Let \(k\) number items let \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) denote item scores. Define total score \(T = \sum_{=1}^k X_i\). Cronbach's alpha can written without matrix notation $$\alpha   \;=\; \frac{k}{k-1}\left(1 - \frac{\sum_{=1}^k   \mathrm{Var}(X_i)}{\mathrm{Var}(T)}\right).$$ words: take sum item variances divide variance total score; subtract ratio 1 multiply \(k/(k-1)\). \(\mathrm{Var}(X_i)\) \(\mathrm{Var}(T)\) computed using pairwise-complete observations. @section Coercion: column coerced via .numeric(). means: factors converted integer level codes (labels); characters parsable numbers become NA; dates/times become underlying numeric representations. Ensure columns truly numeric item responses pre-process needed.
